**Marketing Statement**
NYC Health + Hospitals is the largest public health care system in the United States. We provide essential outpatient, inpatient and home-based services to more than one million New Yorkers every year across the city’s five boroughs. Our large health system consists of ambulatory centers, acute care centers, post-acute care/long-term care, rehabilitation programs, Home Care, and Correctional Health Services. Our diverse workforce is uniquely focused on empowering New Yorkers.
  
  
At NYC Health + Hospitals, our mission is to deliver high quality care health services, without exception. Every employee takes a person-centered approach that exemplifies the ICARE values (Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, and Excellence) through empathic communication and partnerships between all persons.
  
  
**Duties & Responsibilities**
The Contact Center Instructional Designer will design and deliver scalable training programs for our patient support teams. The Instructional Designed will translate complex scheduling processes, Customer Relationship Management (CRM) workflows, and hospital policies into clear, user-friendly learning experiences. This role will ensure that learners are equipped to resolve issues efficiently while providing an empathetic patient experience.
  
  
**General Tasks And Responsibilities Will Include**

- Curriculum Development: Design and maintain engaging New Hire and Continuing Education curricula using adult learning principles.
- Learning Asset Creation: Develop interactive e-learning modules, simulations, facilitator guides, and practical job aids (e.g., Quick Reference Guides, call flows).
- Subject Matter Collaboration: Partner directly with Quality Assurance (QA), Team Managers, and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to identify knowledge gaps and update training in response to product/policy rollouts.
- System Integration: Collaborate with the operations team to align training with core contact center technologies (e.g., Contact Center as a Service -CCaaS- platforms, workforce management tools).
- Measurement & Evaluation: Conduct assessments, analyze program performance metrics, and gather feedback to evaluate the effectiveness of training and iterate on content.
- Project Management: Manage multiple training projects simultaneously, meeting established deadlines without disrupting floor operations.
- Performs other related duties as assigned by Manager, Call Center Training and Quality or Assistant Vice President Contact Center Solutions or Senior Contact Center leadership.

**Minimum Qualifications**

- A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university in Education, Psychology, Personnel Administration, Business Administration, Management or related discipline; and
- One year of experience in employee development and training programs in a health care facility, business, educational, governmental organization or other fields related to training, development and analysis, or training in implementation of operational or management systems; and
- Knowledge of the principles of training, psychology of learning, applications and the ability to instruct and motivate; and
- Ability to communicate orally and relate to others; and
- Proficient writing and research skills; or
- A satisfactory combination of education, training and experience indicating the ability to perform satisfactorily.

**Department Preferences**

- 3-5 years of experience in instructional design, specifically within a corporate training or contact center/customer care environment
- Training
- Instructional Design
- Knowledge Management
- Contact Center
- Healthcare Operations
- Detail-oriented with the ability to properly prioritize, plan and manage time
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Self-motivated with the ability to work independently
- Creative problem solving
- Critical thinking
- Excellent Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, and Excel skills.
- Learning Management Systems
- Contact Center CRM and/or Health EMR
- Computer based training instructional design
- Deep understanding of learning theories (e.g., ADDIE, SAM) and methods to maximize knowledge retention in fast-paced environments.
- Proficiency in rapid authoring tools (e.g., Articulate Storyline 360, Adobe Captivate, Camtasia) and Learning Management Systems (LMS).
- Excellent written and verbal communication, project management abilities, and the capacity to adapt quickly to evolving business needs

**How To Apply**
If you wish to apply for this position, please apply online by clicking the "Apply for Job" button.

**Our mission: e**
liminating every barrier to mental health.
  
  
Spring Health is a global mental health company on a mission to eliminate every barrier to mental health. We're building a world where getting support is simple, personal, and built around the person, so care can continue through every job, move, health plan, and life stage.
  
  
Our AI-native platform helps us deliver personalized support across self-guided tools, coaching, therapy, medication management, and specialty care. With outcomes independently validated by JAMA Network Open and the Validation Institute, Spring Health reaches more than 170 million people worldwide through leading employers, health plans, and partners.
  
  
As an AI-native company, we believe technology should expand the reach, quality, and humanity of care. Every Spring Health team member is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully, apply human judgment to AI outputs, and keep building AI fluency in ways that support their role and our mission.
  
  
Reporting to the Director of Clinical Training, the Clinical Instructional Designer will design and deliver clinical trainings to customers virtually and in person, collaborate in measuring the effectiveness of trainings, and work to grow clinical training offerings. This position will be dedicated to a Spring Health customer and is full time and fully remote.
*Travel will be required up to 30% of the time for in-person training.*
**What You’ll Do**

- Develop clinical content and training materials utilizing modern engagement and instructional design techniques.
- Deliver high-quality clinical trainings in an engaging and impactful manner.
- Partner with customers and internal stakeholders to identify and address specific training needs.
- Utilize the ADDIE model to develop thoughtful curriculum and evaluate the effectiveness of training interventions.
- Maintain strict adherence to Spring Health policies, confidentiality, compliance, and ethical standards.
- Collaborate on the expansion of clinical training offerings and the enhancement of outcome measurements.
- Demonstrate teamwork and adaptability within a fast-paced clinical environment.
- Maintain strong working relationships with customers and internal teams to support unique account requirements.
- Follow all Spring Health policies and maintain strict confidentiality, compliance, and ethical standards.
- Coordinate end-to-end logistics, including building virtual event platforms, selecting clinical providers, preparing materials, and tracking evaluation metrics.
- Work closely with large Jumbo customers to consult on Training and Programming planning, partnering with internal stakeholders to manage and advise accounts.

**What Success Looks Like In This Role**

- Maintain an average feedback rating of 4.5/5 or higher for live events, including on-site delivery.
- Optimize operational efficiency for meeting customer needs related to Clinical Programming and Training.
- Develop deep relationships and a strong cultural understanding of the dedicated customer to ensure trainings feel highly tailored to their workforce.

- An unrestricted clinical license to practice psychotherapy (Psychologist, LCSW, LMFT, LPC, LMHC, etc.). We are unable to accept applications from individuals requiring clinical supervision.
- A minimum of 3 years of post-graduate clinical experience, with at least 1 year of post-licensure experience. Experience with instructional design and content development is required.
- Proven background in corporate training or public speaking, with a strong grasp of adult learning principles, virtual engagement techniques, and training evaluation methods.
- High competency engaging learners virtually; proficient with Google Suite, Zoom, and alternative event/webinar platforms.
- Exceptional verbal and written professional communication skills to engage effectively with corporate customers and fellow Spring Health team members.

Description: A.T. Still University's College of Graduate Studies (ATSU-CGHS) is seeking a full-time, exempt Instructional Designer. This remote position reports to the Instructional Design Manager. The Instructional Designer works as a trusted, consultative partner to faculty subject matter experts (SMEs), bringing instructional design expertise, creativity, and evidence-based recommendations to the development of effective, inclusive courses in CGHS’s fully online programs.The Instructional Designer will manage a portfolio of course development projects where they collaborate closely with faculty SMEs to translate learning outcomes into rigorous and engaging courses, use expertise in learning theory and effective online teaching practices to recommend instructional strategies that advance student success, and integrate educational technologies meaningfully. Additionally, they will contribute to ongoing team operations and broader initiatives to advance teaching and learning across the college.The ideal candidate is both a thoughtful designer and a confident consultant — someone who can listen carefully to understand each program’s needs and adapt their approach as projects evolve. They also embrace opportunities to experiment with new technologies, learn from colleagues, give and receive feedback, and continue growing their practice.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

- Partner with faculty subject matter experts to design, develop, and improve online learning experiences.
- Help faculty translate learning outcomes into effective instructional strategies, activities, assessments, and learning materials.
- Use outcomes-based design, learning theory, adult learning principles, and evidence - based teaching practices to inform your recommendations.
- Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL), accessibility standards, and inclusive teaching practices to create learning experiences that work for diverse learners.
- Assist faculty in creating course content and support faculty with effectively using the Canvas learning management system.
- Integrate other educational technologies when they meaningfully support student learning and stay current with emerging technologies.
- Manage multiple projects with different timelines, priorities, and deliverables, keeping partners informed and projects moving forward.
- Collaborate effectively across the college as part of cross-functional committees and projects.
- Contribute to a feedback-rich team culture by sharing ideas, resources, and expertise with colleagues.

Requirements:

Education & Experience

Required Qualifications

- Master's degree in instructional design, educational technology, curriculum and instruction, or a related field.
- Three or more years of experience in an instructional design or similar role focused on developing online, hybrid, or technology-enhanced learning experiences.
- Three or more years of experience working in higher education settings.
- Adept at applying backward design principles to develop assessments, activities, and instructional materials that are intentionally and transparently aligned with learning outcomes.
- Knowledge of learning theory, adult learning principles, and evidence-based teaching practices.
- Commitment to accessible, inclusive, and learner-centered design.
- Experience collaborating effectively with subject matter experts with varying levels of experience and time.
- Proficiency in authoring in a learning management system (LMS), preferably Canvas.
- Familiarity with Google Workspace (Docs, Slides, Sheets, Calendar, Chat) and Zoom for collaboration.
- Strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and follow through on commitments.
- Coachability and genuine interest in learning, feedback, and professional growth.
- Team orientation and ability to collaborate effectively with a variety of stakeholders.
- Attention to detail and commitment to continuous improvement.
- Ability to work effectively in a remote environment, including self-direction, proactive communication, and comfort collaborating across different (US) time zones.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience teaching or developing courses within healthcare education.
- Advanced knowledge of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), WCAG, Section 508, or other accessibility practices.
- Experience using learning data or other evidence to inform course improvements.
- Proficiency with eLearning software and/or video, audio, and image editing tools.
- Experience leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) in instruction or to streamline workflows.
- Ability to edit web pages using basic HTML code and CSS.

To apply, please submit the following:

1. A resume or CV.

2. A cover letter that clearly addresses: a. Your instructional design experience, including examples of course development

or redesign. b. Your experience with educational technology tools, particularly LMS platforms like Canvas. c. Why you're interested in this role and how you see yourself growing within CGHS.

Applications without cover letters or that do not answer the questions above will not be considered complete. The review of applications will begin October 1, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.

If you have questions about the application process, please contact hiring manager Meri Ellen Lynott at meriellenlynott@atsu.edu. If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability in the application or interview process, please contact ATSU Human Resources for support at 480.219.6130 or 660.626.2113 or email at hr@atsu.edu.

ATSU offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverages, among more. If eligible, employee-elected benefits would begin the first of the month following hire date. For more information, please visit: atsu.edu/employment/benefits.

A.T. Still University (ATSU) does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, ethnicity, national origin, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, age, disability, or veteran status in admission or access to, or treatment or employment in its programs and activities.

**Position Title**
Instructional Designer & Learning Technology Specialist
  
  
**Job Category**
Academic Staff
  
  
**Employment Type**
Terminal (Fixed Term)
  
  
**Job Profile**
Instructional and Media Designer
  
  
**Job Duties**
The University of Wisconsin Oshkosh is seeking a collaborative and innovative Instructional Designer & Learning Technology Specialist to support the READY RURAL initiative. This position serves as the lead for instructional design, educational technology, digital learning, and multimedia development, partnering with faculty and subject matter experts to transform content into engaging, accessible, and workforce-focused learning experiences.
  
  
In this role, you will design and develop high-quality instructional materials for online, hybrid, face-to-face, simulation, mobile, and partner-based learning environments. You will create innovative learning resources that support rural healthcare education, including topics such as telehealth, virtual care, remote patient monitoring, behavioral health, home-based care, interprofessional practice, care coordination, and workforce readiness. The position also supports the development of stackable credentials, continuing education offerings, faculty development resources, and workforce training programs.
  
  
The successful candidate will provide consultation and support to faculty and staff on instructional technologies, digital learning tools, accessibility, and inclusive teaching practices. Responsibilities include developing multimedia resources such as instructional videos, simulations, interactive learning modules, digital toolkits, and tutorials, while ensuring all learning materials meet quality and accessibility standards.
  
  
This position also plays a key role in managing instructional design and media development projects by coordinating timelines, maintaining documentation and reusable resources, training faculty and project personnel on educational technologies, and supporting the collection and interpretation of data to continuously improve learning experiences and program effectiveness.
  
  
Universities of Wisconsin also offers an extremely competitive benefits package for 2026 that includes:
  
  

- Health plans, currently starting at $45 per month.
- 176 hours of vacation per year (prorated for start date).
- 36 hours of personal holiday, and 9 legal holidays (prorated for start date).
- 176 Hours of sick leave for first 18 months. After this period, employees can earn up to 96 hours per fiscal year. Accumulates without limit and does not expire.
- Paid parental leave after six months of continuous employment.
- Wisconsin Retirement System (pension) with 7.2% employer contribution for 2026.

All employment benefits are subject to change. A full list of current benefits and eligibility requirements can be found on our website.
  
  
This position is funded through the READY RURAL grant and is initially offered as a one-year fixed-term appointment. The appointment is renewable annually for up to four years, contingent upon continued grant funding, satisfactory performance, and program needs.
  
  
**Key Job Responsibilities**

- Applies project management principles to course or media design such as defining project scope, establishing milestones, and tracking progress
- Provides pedagogical consultation services for instructors and staff on instructional toolsand technologies, best practices for digital instructional content, and institutional initiatives
- Establishes and maintains collaborative relationships with instructors and other academic staff to advance excellence in teaching and learning
- Reviews courses, media, or other learning products for quality using industry standardsand accessibility best practices
- Trains and supports instructors and staff to leverage technology and teach implement pedagogy effectively
- Works with campus partners across pre-production, production, and post-production stages of media development for implementation in courses and other campusinitiatives
- Creates and maintains documentation on pedagogy, course or media design, templates, instructional technologies, and curates a library of shareable resources
- Designs and develops learning activities and course content using instructional technologies to foster inclusive and equitable student experiences

**Department**
College of Nursing, Health Professions and STEM
  
  
**Compensation**
Starting at $60,000 commensurate with experience
  
  
**Required Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Curriculum and Instruction, Learning Design, Media Production, Healthcare Education, or related field
- Experience designing online, hybrid, technology-enhanced, or multimedia learning experiences.
- Experience with learning management systems, digital learning tools, instructional technologies, or media production tools.
- Experience consulting with faculty, instructors, trainers, or subject matter experts.
- Strong project management, communication, organization, and technical problem-solving skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master’s degree in instructional design, educational technology, learning sciences, curriculum and instruction, healthcare education, or related field.
- Experience supporting healthcare education, simulation-based education, workforce development, continuing education, or academic-practice training.

**Preferred Skills**

- Experience converting instructor-led training into digital or webinar-based formats.
